info.title: bria/fibo
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "bria/fibo", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: The Bria FIBO edit fields, shared by the v1 `POST /proxy/bria/v2/image/edit` request body and the Comfy Router input schema for `bria/fibo`. See the note above this component for why the two surfaces share properties but not `model_version`'s constraints.

guidance_scale.description: Determines how closely the generated image should adhere to the instruction.

images.description: The source image to be edited. Publicly available URL or Base64-encoded. Accepted formats JPEG, JPG, PNG, WEBP. Must contain exactly one item.

instruction.description: Text-based edit instruction (e.g., "make the sky blue", "add a cat"). Either instruction or structured_instruction must be provided.

ip_signal.description: If true, returns a warning for potential IP content in the instruction.

mask.description: Optional mask image URL or Base64-encoded. Black areas will be preserved, white areas will be edited.

model_version.description: The version of the model to use. Comfy Router supplies this from the `{model}` path segment, so omit it there; the value Bria runs is `FIBO`, which the v1 route also defaults to when the field is absent. Not constrained to an enum on this half: Router writes the value in after the caller's body has been validated.

negative_prompt.description: A text prompt specifying concepts, styles, or objects to exclude from the edited image.

prompt_content_moderation.description: If true, returns 422 on instruction moderation failure.

seed.description: Seed for deterministic generation. If omitted, a random seed is used.

structured_instruction.description: A string containing the structured edit instruction in JSON format. Use this instead of instruction for precise, programmatic control.

visual_input_content_moderation.description: If true, returns 422 on images or mask moderation failure.

visual_output_content_moderation.description: If true, returns 422 on visual output moderation failure.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Bria models: the terminal `GET /v2/status/{request_id}` document, forwarded unchanged. Every Bria operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — the submit answers with a `BriaAsyncResponse` handle carrying `request_id`, and Router polls on the caller's behalf (`routerpollstate/families.go` `FamilyBria`), so the body a caller receives is the finished result rather than that handle. All nineteen Bria operations share this one status route and this one document shape.
WHICH FIELD CARRIES THE RESULT DEPENDS ON THE OPERATION, and it is the one thing a caller must not generalise from a sibling model's page. The six image operations — `bria/fibo` and the five `bria/image-edit-*` ids — put the edited image at `result.image_url`. The three `bria/video-edit-*` ids put the edited video at `result.video_url`. `bria/structured-instruction` fills neither URL: it returns the expanded prompt document at `result.structured_prompt`. `routerpollstate`'s `classifyBria` tests those three paths as alternatives, and each model's published example below shows the one its own operation fills.
`result` is present ONLY when `status` is `COMPLETED`, and it also carries `seed`, `prompt` and `refined_prompt`, which are echoes of the REQUEST rather than output — so a caller must key completion off the result LEAF for its operation rather than off `result` being non-empty. `routerpollstate` draws the same line: a `COMPLETED` whose `result` holds only those echoes is `success_without_output`, not a finished generation.
`status` is Bria's own UPPERCASE four-value vocabulary — `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `ERROR`, `UNKNOWN` — and it is not case-folded. `error` is present only when `status` is `ERROR`.

error.description: Error object (only present when status is ERROR)

result.description: Result object (only present when status is COMPLETED)

refined_prompt.description: Refined version of the prompt, or null on a COMPLETED generation Bria did not refine. Nullable because the key is PRESENT carrying null rather than omitted; observed live on bria/image-edit-gen-fill.
